He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]]. He attended [[Pinnacle High School]] in [[Phoenix, Arizona]], where he was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top [[point guard]]s in the 2019 class. Although he mainly grew up in the United States, Mannion represents his birth country of [[Italy national basketball team|Italy]] in international competitions. ==Early life== Mannion was born in [[Siena]], [[Tuscany]], Italy, to former [[NBA]] player [[Pace Mannion]] and Gaia Bianchi. There, he spent his early childhood before his family moved to [[Salt Lake City, Utah]], and finally settled in [[Phoenix, Arizona]].{{cite web |last=Holmes |first=C. J. |title=The Pace Mannion Influence: How Nico draws strength and wisdom from Dad |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1537502/2020/01/16/the-pace-mannion-influence-how-nico-draws-strength-and-wisdom-from-dad/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=January 27, 2020 |date=January 16, 2020}} ==High school career== As a freshman, Mannion began playing basketball for [[Pinnacle High School]] in [[Phoenix, Arizona]] under head coach Charlie Wilde.{{cite web |title=Recruiting Update: Nico Mannion (2020) |url=https://www.prephoops.com/2016/06/recruiting-update-nico-mannion-2020/ |publisher=PrepHoops |access-date=May 5, 2019 |date=June 12, 2016}} On February 9, 2017, he featured in a ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' article, "A 15-Year-Old (Sorta-Maybe) Basketball Prodigy".{{cite magazine |last=Ballard |first=Chris |title=A 15-Year-Old (Sorta-Maybe) Basketball Prodigy |url=https://www.si.com/longform/2017/nico-mannion-high-school-basketball/index.html |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=May 5, 2019 |date=February 9, 2017 |archive-date=November 12, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201112030354/https://www.si.com/longform/2017/nico-mannion-high-school-basketball/index.html |url-status=dead }} Mannion started in all 28 of his games, averaging 20.2 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.7 assists, and 2.4 steals per game while leading Pinnacle to a 22–6 record.{{cite web |title=Nico Mannion |url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/m/mannion-nico.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220428063949/https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/m/mannion-nico.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 28, 2022 |publisher=[[USA Basketball]] |access-date=May 4, 2019 |date=June 4, 2017}} He was named [[MaxPreps]] first team All-American and ''[[The Arizona Republic|Arizona Republic]]'' Class 6A first team All-State.{{cite web |title=2016-17 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Freshman All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/EVB78NqOWEaYDifF0xyXpg/2016-17-maxpreps-boys-basketball-freshman-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=May 5, 2019 |date=April 18, 2017}} Entering his sophomore season, Mannion was named to the ''[[USA Today]]'' All-USA Arizona preseason team. He missed his first four games with a broken left hand.{{cite web |last=Obert |first=Richard |title=Top 50 Arizona high school boys basketball players mid-season rankings |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/11/22/top-50-arizona-high-school-boys-basketball-players-2017-18-season/863054001/ |website=[[The Arizona Republic]] |access-date=May 6, 2019 |date=November 22, 2017}}{{cite web |last=Obert |first=Richard |title=American Family Insurance ALL-USA Arizona preseason boys basketball team 2017-18 |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/all-usa/2017/11/21/american-family-insurance-all-usa-arizona-preseason-boys-basketball-team-2017-18/887161001/ |website=[[The Arizona Republic]] |access-date=May 6, 2019 |date=November 21, 2017}} On February 28, 2018, Mannion scored 21 points in a 76–60 win over [[Mountain Pointe High School]] for the Class 6A state championship.{{cite web |last=Obert |first=Richard |title=Pinnacle boys basketball dominates Mountain Pointe for 6A title |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2018/02/28/pinnacle-boys-basketball-dominates-mountain-pointe-6-title/383985002/ |website=[[The Arizona Republic]] |access-date=May 6, 2019 |date=February 28, 2018}} He finished the season averaging 23.4 points, 4.7 rebounds, and 5.8 assists per game, leading Pinnacle to a 24–7 record.{{cite web |last=Divens |first=Jordan |title=2017-18 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Sophomore All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/yL1wLxRGiUeRCLlOOrsePA/2017-18-maxpreps-boys-basketball-sophomore-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=May 6, 2019 |date=April 17, 2018}} Mannion received MaxPreps Sophomore All-American third team and Arizona [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] distinction.{{cite web |title=Nico Mannion 2017 - 2018 Arizona Boys Basketball Player of the Year |url=https://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/winner/nico-mannion/36417 |publisher=[[Gatorade]] |access-date=May 6, 2019 |archive-date=March 17, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180317173015/http://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/winner/nico-mannion/36417 |url-status=dead }} He took online summer courses to be able to graduate in the following spring.{{cite magazine |last=West |first=Jenna |title=Five-Star Recruit Nico Mannion Reclassifies From 2020 to 2019 Class |url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/07/20/nico-mannion-reclassify-2019-class-five-star-recruit |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=May 7, 2019 |date=July 20, 2018}} On December 1, Mannion scored 37 points, including the game-winning three-pointer, in an 82–80 victory over [[Shadow Mountain High School]], who had won 73 straight games against Arizona opponents.{{cite web |last=Divens |first=Jordan |title=Nico Mannion, Pinnacle knock off No. 13 Shadow Mountain to snap 73-game Arizona win streak |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/x5DYRWwP_kmpPkaD-Cq1Eg/nico-mannion,-pinnacle-knock-off-no-13-shadow-mountain-to-snap-73-game-arizona-win-streak.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=May 8, 2019 |date=November 30, 2018}}{{cite web |title=Mannion's buzzer-beater lifts Pinnacle past Shadow Mountain |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2018/11/30/shadow-mountain-pinnacle-boys-basketball/2165597002/ |website=[[The Arizona Republic]] |access-date=May 8, 2019 |date=November 30, 2018}} MaxPreps writer Jordan Divens said that Mannion's performance in the game "will go down in Arizona high school basketball lore." Five days later, Mannion recorded 33 points and 12 assists in a nationally televised game against top recruit [[Jalen Green]] and [[San Joaquin Memorial High School]] at the Hoophall West Invitational.{{cite web |last=Obert |first=Richard |title=Nico Mannion puts on a show against top-rated Jalen Green in Pinnacle rout |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2018/12/06/pinnacles-nico-mannion-puts-show-against-top-rated-jalen-green/2221224002/ |website=[[The Arizona Republic]] |access-date=May 8, 2019 |date=December 6, 2018}} On December 30, he scored 45 points in an 88–78 loss to [[Mater Dei High School (Santa Ana, California)|Mater Dei High School]] at the Rancho Mirage Holiday Invitational National Division championship.{{cite web |last=John |first=Andrew L. |title=Mater Dei overcomes Nico Mannion's 45 points to win Rancho Mirage Invitational title |url=https://www.desertsun.com/story/sports/basketball/2018/12/30/mater-dei-overcomes-nico-mannions-45-points-win-rancho-mirage-title/2444525002/ |website=[[The Desert Sun]] |access-date=May 8, 2019 |date=December 30, 2018}} Mannion, on February 2, 2019, tallied 57 points, including the game-winning shot as time expired, to help defeat [[Chaparral High School (Arizona)|Chaparral High School]].{{cite web |last=Pascoe |first=Bruce |title=Arizona Wildcats signee Nico Mannion scores 57 in high school senior night game |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/arizona-wildcats-signee-nico-mannion-scores-in-high-school-senior/article_3d39d270-26a8-11e9-88f7-df0f3e133788.html |website=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |access-date=May 8, 2019 |date=February 2, 2019}} On February 27, he led Pinnacle to a second Class 6A state title, posting 56 points, eight rebounds, and six assists in an 83–64 win over Chaparral High School.{{cite web |last=Kelapire |first=Ryan |title=Nico Mannion, Pinnacle capture second straight 6A state championship |url=https://www.azdesertswarm.com/basketball/2019/2/26/18242542/nico-mannion-pinnacle-state-championship-chaparral-highlights-arizona-basketball-recruiting-2019 |publisher=Arizona Desert Swarm |access-date=May 8, 2019 |date=February 26, 2019}} By the end of the season, Mannion was averaging 43.4 points, 6.2 rebounds, and 6.2 assists per game.{{cite web |last=Obert |first=Richard |title=Pinnacle's Nico Mannion receives national basketball honor |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/04/08/arizona-bound-nico-mannion-named-national-seniors-hs-basketball-poy/3405334002/ |website=[[The Arizona Republic]] |access-date=May 8, 2019 |date=April 8, 2019}} He reclaimed the Arizona Gatorade Player of the Year award and was recognized as National High School Coaches Association (NHSCA) Senior Athlete of the Year.{{cite web |last=Potter |first=Mattie |title=Arizona's Mannion named 2018-2019 Boys' Basketball Athlete of the Year |url=https://www.nhsca.com/news/445693/info@nhsca.com |publisher=National High School Coaches |date=March 15, 2019}} Mannion also earned ''USA Today'' All-USA second team and [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year Award|Naismith]] All-American third team honors.{{cite web |title=2018-19 ALL-USA Green, Nico Mannion score 8 points apiece in McDonald's All-American Game |url=https://www.azdesertswarm.com/basketball/2019/3/27/18284770/josh-green-nico-mannion-mcdonalds-all-american-game-stats-highlights-box-score-arizona-wildcats |publisher=Arizona Desert Swarm |date=April 14, 2019}} ===Recruiting=== Mannion was considered a top 20 prospect in the 2020 recruiting class by [[247Sports]], [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] and [[ESPN]]. But he [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] to the 2019 class. Mannion received his first [[college basketball]] offer from [[Cal State Northridge Matadors men's basketball|Cal State Northridge]] while in eighth grade.{{cite web |last=Bossi |first=Eric |title=Sharp shooting 2020 PG Nico Mannion holds several offers |url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/usa-bball-sharp-shooting-2020-pg-nico-mannion-holds-several-offers |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=May 5, 2019 |date=June 4, 2017}} In high school, he picked up offers from several major [[NCAA Division I]] programs, including [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] and [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]].{{cite web |title=Nico Mannion |url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/226820 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=May 7, 2019}} Mannion was a consensus five-star recruit and the best recruit from Arizona in the 2019 class.{{cite web |title=Nico Mannion, Pinnacle, Point Guard |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Nico-Mannion-46035982/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com]] |access-date=May 7, 2019}}{{cite web |title=Nico Mannion, 2019 Point guard |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2019/nico-mannion-181233 |publisher=[[Rivals.com]] |access-date=May 7, 2019 |archive-date=March 21, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321111439/https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2019/nico-mannion-181233 |url-status=dead }} On September 14, 2018, he committed to [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] over [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]].{{cite web |last=Biancardi |first=Paul |author-link=Paul Biancardi |title=No. 2 PG recruit Nico Mannion chooses overall = 8 | rivals overall = 14 | espn overall = 9 | accessdate = April 5, 2019 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Mannion earned preseason first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12 Conference]] honors and was named to the preseason watch lists for the [[John R. Wooden Award|Wooden Award]] and [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Trophy]].{{cite web |title=Pac-12 unveils inaugural men's basketball preseason All-Conference teams |url=https://pac-12.com/news/2019/10/8/pac-12-unveils-inaugural-mens-basketball-preseason-all-conference-teams.aspx |publisher=[[Pac-12 Conference]] |access-date=January 27, 2020 |date=October 7, 2019}} In his second collegiate game for [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], on November 6, 2019, he recorded 23 points, nine assists and four rebounds in a 90–69 win over [[2019–20 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]].{{cite web |last=Pascoe |first=Bruce |title=Freshmen Nico Mannion, Josh Green lead Arizona past Illinois |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/college/ua/2019/11/10/freshmen-nico-mannion-josh-green-lead-arizona-past-illinois/2559940001/ |website=[[The Arizona Republic]] |access-date=January 27, 2020 |date=November 10, 2019}} On November 28, Mannion posted 16 points and 11 assists and made a game-winning [[layup]] with four seconds left in a 93–91 victory over [[2019–20 Pepperdine Waves men's basketball team|Pepperdine]] in the first round of the [[Wooden Legacy]].{{cite web |date=November 29, 2019 |title=Nico Mannion's last-second layup saves No. 14 Arizona against Pepperdine (VIDEO) |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/college-basketball/news/nico-mannions-last-second-layup-saves-no-14-arizona-against-pepperdine-video |access-date=November 30, 2023 |website=nbcsports.com |publisher=[[Associated Press]]}} In a second-round win over [[2019–20 Penn Quakers men's basketball team|Penn]], he scored a season-high 24 points. Mannion led his team to the Wooden Legacy title and was named tournament [[most valuable player]] (MVP) after averaging 16.3 points and 7.3 assists per game. In the following day, he earned Pac-12 freshman of the week accolades.{{cite web |title=Martin, Mannion collect Pac-12 Men's Basketball weekly honors |url=https://pac-12.com/article/2019/12/02/martin-mannion-collect-pac-12-mens-basketball-weekly-honors |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191202212813/https://pac-12.com/article/2019/12/02/martin-mannion-collect-pac-12-mens-basketball-weekly-honors |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 2, 2019 |publisher=[[Pac-12 Conference]] |access-date=January 27, 2020 |date=December 2, 2019}} On February 29, 2020, Mannion had 19 points and six assists in a 69–64 loss to [[2019–20 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|UCLA]].{{cite news |last=Pascoe |first=Bruce |title=On Sean Miller's 'conversations' with officials at UCLA, Josh Green's absence and silver linings |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/on-sean-miller-s-conversations-with-officials-at-ucla-josh/article_ccff0fe8-5b8f-11ea-84c5-e32b03bfe40c.html |access-date=March 1, 2020 |work=[[Arizona Daily Star]] |date=March 1, 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Mannion was named to the [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] second team and the All-Freshman Team.{{Cite web|url=https://pac-12.com/article/2020/03/08/2019-20-pac-12-mens-basketball-all-conference-awards-announced|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200326010600/https://pac-12.com/article/2020/03/08/2019-20-pac-12-mens-basketball-all-conference-awards-announced|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 26, 2020|title=Pac-12 announces 2019-20 Men's Basketball annual major awards|date=March 9, 2020|website=pac-12.com|access-date=March 9, 2020}} Mannion averaged 14.0 points and 5.3 assists per game as a freshman. Following the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last=Smith |first=Keith |title=Arizona's Nico Mannion to declare for 2020 NBA Draft |url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2020/03/08/nico-mannion-nba-draft/ |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=March 8, 2020|access-date=March 25, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Golden State Warriors (2020–2021)=== Mannion was selected with the 48th overall pick by the [[Golden State Warriors]] in the [[2020 NBA draft]] hosted on November 18, 2020.{{cite web |last=Grinfelds |first=Dzintars |date=November 19, 2020 |title=Get to Know the Dubs' 2020 NBA Draft Picks |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news-blogs/get-to-know-2020-draft-picks |access-date=November 30, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} Mannion made 30 appearances (including one start) for Golden State during the [[2020–21 NBA season]], recording averages of 4.1 points, 1.5 rebounds, and 2.3 assists.{{Cite web|title=Nico Mannion 2020-21 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4431672/nico-mannion|access-date=June 29, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} After one season with the Warriors and after playing with the [[Italian national basketball team]] at the [[Basketball at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2020 Summer Olympics]], he opted to leave the United States for [[Virtus Bologna]].{{cite news |last1=Dupont |first1=Zach |title=Nico Mannion to Leave Golden State Warriors for Italian League |url=https://www.slamonline.com/news/nba/nico-mannion-to-leave-golden-state-warriors-for-italian-league/ |access-date=12 January 2024 |work=[[Slam (magazine)|SLAM]] |date=12 August 2021 |language=en}} ===Virtus Bologna (2021–2023)=== On August 10, 2021, Mannion signed a two-year contract with Italian club [[Virtus Bologna]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]],{{cite web |date=August 10, 2021 |title=NICO MANNION IS A NEW PLAYER OF VIRTUS SEGAFREDO BOLOGNA |url=https://www.virtus.it/en/news/nico-mannion-new-player-of-virtus-segafredo-bologna/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210810170659/https://www.virtus.it/en/news/nico-mannion-new-player-of-virtus-segafredo-bologna/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 10, 2021 |website=virtus.it}} a team with the ambition of winning the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] and qualify to the [[EuroLeague]]. The deal was closed in 24 hours after the end of the [[free agency]].{{cite web |date=August 10, 2021 |title=Nico Mannion alla Virtus Bologna: che colpaccio |url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Basket/SerieA/10-08-2021/nico-mannion-virtus-bologna-420340520518.shtml |access-date=November 30, 2023 |website=gazzetta.it |language=it}} After having ousted [[BC Lietkabelis|Lietkabelis]], [[Ratiopharm Ulm|Ulm]] and [[Valencia Basket|Valencia]] in the first three rounds of the [[2022 EuroCup Basketball Playoffs|playoffs]], on May 11, 2022, Virtus defeated [[Bursaspor Basketbol|Frutti Extra Bursaspor]] by 80–67 at the Segafredo Arena, winning its first [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] and qualifying for the [[EuroLeague]] after 14 years.{{cite web |title=Game Night: Virtus is the 7DAYS EuroCup champion and headed back to the EuroLeague! |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/news/game-night-a-new-7days-eurocup-champ-is-crowned-tonight/?pageTitle=Homepage&historyUrl=/eurocup/ |website=euroleaguebasketball.net |date=11 May 2022 |access-date=May 12, 2022 |archive-date=May 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220511221231/https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/news/game-night-a-new-7days-eurocup-champ-is-crowned-tonight/?pageTitle=Homepage&historyUrl=/eurocup/ |url-status=dead }} However, despite having ended the regular season at the first place and having ousted 3–0 both [[U.S. Victoria Libertas Pallacanestro|Pesaro]] and [[Derthona Basket|Tortona]] in the first two rounds of playoffs, Virtus was defeated 4–2 in the national finals by [[Olimpia Milano]].{{cite web |date=June 18, 2022 |title=Olimpia Milano campione d'Italia, Virtus Bologna ko 81-64 in gara-6 |url=https://sport.sky.it/basket/serie-a/2022/06/18/olimpia-milano-virtus-bologna-risultato |access-date=November 30, 2023 |website=Sky Sport |language=it}} On September 29, 2022, after having ousted Milano in the semifinals, Virtus won its [[2022 Italian Basketball Supercup|third Supercup]], defeating 72–69 [[Dinamo Sassari|Banco di Sardegna Sassari]] and achieving a back-to-back, following the 2021 trophy.{{cite web |title=Supercoppa, trionfa la Virtus Bologna! Canestro decisivo di Mickey, Sassari cede 72-69|url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Basket/SerieA/29-09-2022/basket-supercoppa-trionfa-virtus-bologna-sassari-ko-72-69-450409276762.shtml|website=Gazzetta dello Sport|date=29 September 2022}} However, despite good premises Virtus ended the [[2022–23 EuroLeague|EuroLeague season]] at 14th place, thus it did not qualify for the playoffs.[https://bolognabasket.org/virtus-il-punto-a-fine-eurolega/ Virtus, il punto a fine EuroLega]. BolognaBasket Moreover, the team was defeated in the [[Italian Basketball Cup]] final by [[Pallacanestro Brescia|Brescia]]. {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Mannion is the son of an American father and an Italian mother. His father, [[Pace Mannion]], is a former [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) player who played for six NBA teams through the 1980s.{{cite web |title=Pace Mannion Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/mannipa01.html |publisher=[[Sports Reference]] |access-date=April 30, 2019}} He played professionally for various teams in Italy until his retirement in 2002.{{cite web |last=Melloni |first=Mirco |title=L'Italia ha il suo Mamba: la storia di Nico Mannion, fenomeno delle giovanili azzurre |url=https://www.lastampa.it/2017/08/14/sport/litalia-ha-il-suo-mamba-la-storia-di-nico-mannion-fenomeno-delle-giovanili-azzurre-fA4EOLFEezmgTsLco7Wz3L/pagina.html |website=[[La Stampa]] |access-date=April 30, 2019 |language=it |date=August 14, 2017}}{{cite web |last=Frangipani |first=Niccolò |title=Astri Nascenti nel Basket: Nico Mannion, the italian stallion |url=http://www.vita-sportiva.it/2018/08/11/nico-mannion-the-italian-stallion/ |publisher=Vita Sportiva |access-date=April 30, 2019 |date=August 11, 2018 }}{{Dead link|date=December 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} Most notably, he helped Italian club [[Pallacanestro Cantù]] win the [[1990–91 FIBA Korać Cup|1991 FIBA Korać Cup]]. Mannion's mother, [[Gaia Bianchi]], is a former [[volleyball]] player who played for the [[Italy women's national volleyball team|Italian national volleyball team]].{{cite web |last=Boivin |first=Paola |title=Boivin: Pinnacle freshman Nico Mannion creating national buzz |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2016/12/14/boivin-pinnacle-prodigy-mannion-creating-buzz-nice-pace-basketball/95442212/ |website=[[The Arizona Republic]] |access-date=April 30, 2019 |date=December 14, 2016}} In high school, one of Mannion's teammates was current New Orleans Saints quarterback [[Spencer Rattler]].
